CITY OF LA VERNE
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  HELD VIA TELECONFERENCE
  Wednesday, March 17, 2021

1.  Chairperson Simison called the regular meeting of the La Verne Planning
  Commission to order at 6:32 p.m. He stated that all comments should be sent to
  planning@cityoflaverne.org.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chairperson Simison led the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL: Planning Commissioners present: Thomas Allison, Jason Lorge,
  Phil May and Jason Simison. Not present: Jeff Allred (due to a conflict of
  interest). Advisory personnel present: Community Development Director Eric
  Scherer, City Attorney Bob Kress, Principal Planner Candice Bowcock, Deputy
  City Engineer Cody Howing and Secretary Natalie Hiatt. Others present: John
  Leveille, Christine Donoghue, Bryan Crawford, Matt Waken, James Kawamura,
  and Art Alvarado.

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  None

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

6.  CASE NOS. 20-20ZC, 109-20SP, 19-20GPA, AND 18-20TTM – A
  PROPOSAL TO DEVELOP 42 SINGLE FAMILY HOMES AT 2820
  AMHERST STREET (8666-021-902) AND A PORTION OF THE
  ADJACENT PARCEL, 8666-021-904, BOTH CITY-OWNED
  PROPERTIES. THE PROPERTIES ARE CURRENTLY ZONED PR3D
  AND ARE DESIGNATED LOW DENSITY RESIDENTIAL IN THE
  GENERAL PLAN.

  RESOLUTION NO. 1270
 Planning Commission Minutes
March 17, 2021
  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  RECOMMENDING APPROVAL TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR CASE
  NO. 18-20TTM, VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP 83064, 109-20SP,
  ADOPTION OF THE “AMHERST COLLECTION SPECIFIC PLAN”, 20-
  20ZC, A ZONE CHANGE FROM PR3D TO SPECIFIC PLAN, AND 19-
  20GPA, A GENERAL PLAN AMMENDMENT CHANGING THE SITE
  FROM LOW DENSITY RESIDENTIAL TO MEDIUM DENSITY
  RESIDENTIAL. REQUESTS BY MJW INVESTMENTS, LLC, FOR A 5.6
  ACRE PARCEL LOCATED AT 2820 AMHERST STREET (8666-021-902)
  AND A PORTION OF THE ADJACENT PARCEL, 8666-021-904
  CREATING A 42 SINGLE FAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENT
  AND ADOPTING THE PREPARED ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT
  REPORT FOR THE PROJECT.

  Principal Planner Candice Bowcock presented her report.

  Chairperson Simison opened the Public Hearing.

  Matt Waken presented a market study report.

  Christine Donoghue of Rincon Consultants, Inc. presented the environmental
  process.

  Bryan Crawford presented a traffic analysis study outlining the process, approach,
  and methodology.

  There were 32 public comments received via email. The following individuals
  participated via Zoom or by telephone:

  Sue Geddes
  Patti Latourelle
  Matthew Uyboco
  Janine Johnston
  Hector Ramirez
  Denise Fisher
  Andres Aldana
  Danita Beauchamp
  Cynthia Galbadon
  Ruth Spathias
  Cheryl DiGiulio
  Liz Arenas
  Jeff Allred
  Joe Galbadon
  MD Shaheed

  2
 Planning Commission Minutes
March 17, 2021
  Chairperson Simison closed the Public Hearing.

  Commissioner Allison expressed concerns for the economic impact and home
  values.

  Mr. Waken explained how it is expected to benefit the neighborhood home
  values.

  Commissioner Allison expressed concern with the traffic due to the size and
  location of the project as it sits away from the main street.

  Mr. Howing and Mr. Leveille proceeded to explain the process of the traffic study
  at the local level.

  Commissioner Lorge stated that the traffic analysis seemed flawed due to the
  density.

  Chairperson Simison asked for responses to several public comments. Mr. Scherer
  and Mr. Crawford responded to the comments.

  It was moved by Commissioner Allison to recommend approval of Resolution
  1270. The motion failed due to a lack of a second.

  It was moved by Commissioner Allison and seconded by Commissioner May to
  recommend denial of the project. The Commission stated that they would be
  supportive of the development at a lower density. Motion carried by a 4-0 vote.

OTHER MATTERS/INFORMATION

  None

ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 8:56 p.m. The next regular meeting of the Planning
  Commission will be held April 14, 2021 at 6:30 p.m.
